title: Dynamic region preference using percentile-latency gradients and network error signals
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current region routing uses coarse health scores and static thresholds which react slowly to emerging latency degradations or transient network errors. This ticket designs and implements a telemetry-driven region preference algorithm that blends percentile latency gradients (p50/p95 deltas), short-term error signals (retransmits, TCP RTOs, HTTP 5xx rates), and per-region capacity tier preferences to select the best region and fallback model variant for each request. Goal is to reduce observed tail latency for end-users while keeping quality regressions under a configurable threshold when falling back to smaller/quantized model variants.
acceptance_criteria: A region preference score calculated per region at 30s cadence that combines p50 and p95 gradients, normalized by baseline and smoothed with EWMA
When score exceeds degrade threshold, routing decisions favor lower-latency region or fallback model variant under policy rules (see implementation notes)
Simulated traffic tests show p95 user-facing latency reduced by >=12% on injected network jitter scenarios compared to baseline score-based routing
Canary rollout (5% traffic) completed without customer-facing errors for 24h, metrics and alerts validated
Docs: runtime config schema and Console UI toggles added to routing policy page
decision_log: 2026-02-21: Chosen core signal set = {p50, p95, TCP retransmit rate, HTTP 5xx rate, packet loss proxy via retransmits}. Decided against using raw RTT from client due to measurement noise and attribution complexity.

2026-02-24: Scoring function decided: score = alpha*percentile_gradient + beta*error_signal where percentile_gradient = normalized((p95-p50)/baseline_p50) and error_signal is capped EWMA of retransmits and 5xx rate.

2026-02-26: Fallback policy: prefer same-model quantized variants if quality drift < quality_budget; otherwise route to different region with compatible model family. Quality checks use offline eval set and a small production prompt set sampled per tenant.
2026-02-28: Chosen smoothing and TTL: EWMA half-life = 45s, decision TTL = 60s to prevent flapping. Anomaly suppression window of 3m for transient spikes.
implementation_notes: Telemetry pipeline: add new derived metrics in metrics-service: p50_gradient, p95_gradient, retransmit_rate_ewma (1m, 5m), http5xx_ewma
Scoring service: new microservice 'region-scoring' reads metrics store at 15-30s intervals, outputs per-region score and reason codes to routing-control-plane

Routing control-plane changes: support per-request region preference hints plus TTL and reason codes for observability. Control-plane evaluates policy with weights from runtime config stored in configstore.

Fallback model selection: model-compatibility matrix to be extended with quality_cost_metric and quantized_variant_quality_delta. Routing policy must consult this matrix and enforce quality_budget per-tenant (default 0.02 loss in BLEU/embedding-similarity proxy).
SDK/API: no client changes required. Expose opt-out/override header and route hint for enterprise customers via Console toggle.
Testing: end-to-end test harness will run Chaos scenarios (packet loss, cross-region peering flaps) against staging clusters to validate behavior and flapping protections.

Observability: add structured logs for each decision, include contributing signals, current EWMA values, and chosen action (route/fallback/hold). Add dashboard with decision outcomes, action counts, and per-tenant quality drift.
RBAC & safety: score emission and routing decisions limited to control-plane service accounts. Audit logs enabled for all decision mutations.
metrics: primary: user-facing p50, p95, p99 latency by region
secondary: routing action distribution (same-region, region-failover, model-fallback)
safety: quality-delta per tenant (offline eval proxies & live LLM-sampled prompts)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): simulate 3 synthetic failure modes for 72h, validate metrics and suppressed flaps
Phase 1 (canary): 5% production traffic for non-enterprise tenants, 24h observe/pass criteria
Phase 2 (ramp): 25% for 48h with automated rollback on threshold breaches (p95 increase >5% or error-rate spike >2x),
Phase 3 (wide): 100% enable with per-tenant opt-out; monitor first 72h closely; post-mortem window 1 week
Rollback triggers: routing decision error >0.1% (invalid preferences), sudden quality-delta > configured budget, or unexplained region flapping > 1 event per 5m
